review_notes: I read the whole file. I also read the related uses of the head-operator simp lemmas in Leakage.lean, CostGeometry.lean and Clipping.lean. Most of the file is inequality proofs closed by nlinarith, and it has little simp surface. The existing simp lemmas (`linearHead_equiv`, `linearOuterHead_apply`, and the quadratic versions) are rfl-based and oriented correctly, since they push application inward to the `head` normal form. I found no loops or competing rules. The one weakness is that no simp-usable lemma states what `P x = x` means componentwise, so each use rebuilds it by hand. I did not run Lean, so the proposed lemma is untested. I also saw that `head_idem` and the `*_idem` lemmas are not simp, and I did not report that: the simp-set effect is unclear, and nothing here shows the lemmas would fire usefully.

findings.problem: The hypothesis `linearOuterHead D hD x = x` is turned into a per-coordinate fixed-point statement by hand. Each use applies `congrArg (fun z => linearBlockEquiv (n+1) (z n))` and then `simpa only` with the apply and equiv simp lemmas. The quadratic twin repeats this, and `activeHead_center` and `mem_active_tail` in CostGeometry.lean do the same kind of unfolding. The simp set has no lemma that rewrites `P x = x` or `P x = 0` into the form `head (D n) (blockEquiv (x n)) = blockEquiv (x n)`. Every caller has to rediscover the congrArg and simpa recipe, and each one fixes its own simp-only list.
findings.proposed_change: Add one componentwise characterisation per family, for example `linearOuterHead_eq_self_iff : linearOuterHead D hD x = x ↔ ∀ n, head (D n) (linearBlockEquiv (n+1) (x n)) = linearBlockEquiv (n+1) (x n)`. Add the analogous `= 0` statement and the quadratic versions. Prove them from `lp.ext_iff`, `linearBlockEquiv (n+1)).injective`, `linearOuterHead_apply` and `linearHead_equiv`. Tag them `@[simp]` if the simp-set effect is acceptable, otherwise use them with `rw` or `simp only`. Then `hxn` becomes `(linearOuterHead_eq_self_iff D hD).1 hx n`.
findings.benefit: The several hand-written congrArg and simpa blocks reduce to one lemma application. The linear and quadratic proofs stay in sync. Later files get a stable normal form for 'x is fixed by the head' instead of re-deriving it.

evidence.excerpt: have hh := congrArg (fun z : QuadraticOuter => z n) hx
